steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Cream butter, brown sugar, and white sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until fluffy. Beat in one egg at a time, then stir in vanilla.

Combine flour, cinnamon, salt, and baking soda in a separate bowl; stir into the creamed mixture. Mix in oats and walnuts until just blended. Drop teaspoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, about 12 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Excellent Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These chewy oatmeal cookies studded with walnuts and spiced with a hint of delicious cinnamon are a favorite treat for dessert or an after-school snack.
raw_recipe.name: Excellent Oatmeal Cookies

review.reviewBody: These are absolutely delicious! I read that some reviewers' cookies were coming apart, so I added 1/8 c extra flour as recommended and I made sure that I rolled the cookies into tight balls before placing on cookie sheet. I also reduced salt by half, due to reviews that the cookies were too salty. Will make again and again!

I am a great cookie/baker, it’s my specialty. Had a request for oatmeal, and decided to try a new recipe, after using a couple others from this site for years. This is hands-down the BEST oatmeal cookie recipe, the caveat being to use the alterations in the comments (extra flour and oats, less salt, baked at 350°), along with using 1/2 shortening, 1/2 butter. I portioned out my cookies onto a cookie sheet using a Pampered Chef scoop- it makes big cookies. I refrigerated overnight, and baked right from the fridge. Halfway through I used a fork to lightly flatten the cookies, then returned to the oven. Mine took approx 15 minutes to bake, I pulled when the edges were very light brown and let them cool on the cookie sheet. The texture is off-the-charts; both crispy and chewy. I added walnuts and dried fruit (raisins, crans, blueberries, cherries), and a little almond extract in addition to the vanilla. I double the recipe, portion, refrigerate, then baggie up and freeze. Thanks for the great recipe!!!

Very NICE recipe! The vanilla and cinnamon give it a wonderful flavor. I was determined to follow as written but I got concerned when mixing the ingredients about the amount of salt and the amount of flour-so I added about 1/8 cup of flour and went with 1/2 tsp of salt instead of a whole tsp. Also, I substituted a couple of handfulls of raisins for the nuts. I used a larger spoon when dropping the dough, and wound up adjusting the cooking time to 16 minutes. I am a firm believer in lining pans with parchment paper, so when I was tinkering with the timing I kept checking until I could see that the tops of the cookies were not glossy anymore and the edges around the bottom were lightly browned-this yields a moist cookie with a faint crispness at the bottom which is my idea of cookie heaven. These cookies turned out beautifully and this recipe is now officially how I will obtain my oatmeal raisin cookie fix for the rest of my life. Good one, thanks for sharing!

Awesome! I doubled the recipe and dropped by tablespoon instead of teaspoon and added a smidge more cinnamon and a 1/4 tsp of cloves but followed everything else exactly. It took 15 mins for soft centers and slightly crunchy edges. They came out perfect. Next time I am going to add chopped praline pecans.

Wish i could give them 10 stars! One of the best oatmeal cookie recipes we've ever tried! The ingredients take just a few minutes to put together and the cookies bake up beautifully!! And this is coming from someone who is without her Kitchenaide stand mixer and oven right now!! I whipped this recipe up by hand, and baked the cookies in my Black and Decker toaster oven. I had to let the cookies bake a little longer (about 5-10 minutes more) just because I was using a toaster oven. But my daughter couldn't wait to devour them as soon as they were done!! I divided my batter in half and added raisins to the first half, and chocolate chips to the other half. ??

I made these exactly per the recipe except I used regular oats instead of quick-cooking oats, since that was all I had. I pulsed the oats, 1 cup at a time in food processor, until the oats were about 1/2 original size. These cookies were excellent. I will make them the same way next time. I may try pecans next time, although the walnuts were delicious, too. The cookies did "come apart" slightly immediately after baking, but they "came back together" after cooling. Just use a nice thin, flat spatula to remove from cookie sheet. I tossed in 1/2 cup raisins. Yum! Thanks for sharing, Beatrice.

In an effort to make my husband and daughter a healthier cookie, I changed a few ingredients - AND WE LOVE 'EM! Substituted a 1/2 cup almond flour for some of the regular flour; substituted coconut oil for half the butter; substituted liquid Stevia for the white sugar (verify equivalencies); used regular oats instead of quick-cook; added 3/4 cup chopped carrots; baked them for 15 minutes. Moist, substantial and delicious.

Made as others suggested by increasing flour to 1.5 cups and baking soda to 1 teaspoon. Then I chilled the dough before forming into balls and they cooked fine, not flat. I made may balls larger than suggested about a large tablespoon and cooked for 18 minutes at 325. They came out perfect . The taste is still a touch less buttery than I like, might add more butter next time

Great recipe with a lot of flexibility to change spices and additions. I pack my flour when scooping and have had no issues with them falling apart. I'm also partial to pecans so used a package of them chopped. I use a 2tbs cookie scoop as I want a substantial cookie. I bake for 18 min to ensre they firm up. I get a 2.5 dozen yield.

These are beyond good. They are even better the second day. I am mad at myself for making them (and eating about two dozen!). I added 1/8 cup of flower and pounded the walnuts to smithereens, in a baggy with a soup can, before adding them. So buttery and texturally ideal.
A good plain oatmeal cookie. I baked for 14 mins. and used half coconut oil and half butter. Could add chocolate chips or raisins.
I added Craisins. They turned out too good. All Gone. 👍

These cookies are delicious!! I followed the recipe exact, and they came out perfect. My oven is fairly new and burns a little hot, so I baked them for 8 minutes then checked them, added another minute and that was it. I removed them from the oven but left them on the pan for another ten minutes while the next batch baked. Keeping them on the pan before transferring to the cooling rack helps them set, and they came out perfect. Don’t forget to use parchment paper!
Great easy recipe but reduced sugar..only used 1/2 cup brown sugar Added 2 tbsp Tahini in place of nuts.
YUM I USED CHOCOLATE COVERED RAISINS...
I didn't put walnuts and I used baking powder instead of baking soda and it tastes amazing!

Loved it! I reversed the salt and baking soda ratios; used 1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp of salt instead . It seemed like it might have been a typo mistake. Came out great and the recipe is easy to follow.
Wow, just wonderful, and I thank you for this recipe, Beatrice. This is my first time making these. I baked off a half batch, then added currants to the other half. Also good. (No raisins on hand.)
